sections.rawHeading: 1 · Licensing (GOV — high confidence; genuine state license)
sections.title: State licensing and registration
sections.markdown: **Utah DOES license contractors statewide** through the **Division of Professional Licensing (DOPL — renamed from the Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing)**, Dept. of Commerce, under the **Construction Trades Licensing Act (Utah Code Title 58, Chapter 55; rules at Utah Admin. Code R156-55a).** Chimney/masonry work maps to a **specialty (S-class) license — S230, "Masonry, Siding, Stucco, Glass, and Rain Gutter Contractor,"** or, for whole-building work spanning trades, the general building **B100** classification. Licensure requires a **qualifier with experience, passing the trade/specialty exam plus the Utah Contractor Business & Law exam (and a pre-licensure business/law course), proof of insurance, and workers'-comp/registration compliance.** So unlike Colorado or Illinois, Utah gives you **a state credential to look up.** Public lookup: **secure.utah.gov/llv/search/index.html** (DOPL Licensee Lookup and Verification System; verified Sep 15, 2026); program info at commerce.utah.gov/dopl. Unlicensed contracting is a violation subject to DOPL enforcement. **Sweep-only work is exempt:** DOPL's rule lists "chimney sweepers other than repairing masonry" among activities determined not to significantly impact public health and therefore not requiring a contractor license — **Utah Admin. Code R156-55a-301(7)(n)** (LII mirror of the Utah Admin. Code, rule last amended eff. 1/3/2023; law.cornell.edu/regulations/utah/Utah-Admin-Code-R156-55a-301, checked Sep 15, 2026). Masonry repair by a sweep is NOT exempt. **Stove/fireplace installs:** the **S330 Landscape and Recreation** classification's construction scope (subpart (3)(b) as printed on the mirror) includes "metal fireboxes, fireplaces, and wood or coal-burning stoves, including the installation of venting and exhaust systems, if the individual performing the installation is RMGA-certified," while S330 excludes electrical, plumbing and natural-gas-related work (same source). **Small-job exemption (statute):** Utah Code **§ 58-55-305(1)(h)** exempts alteration/repair/improvement with a contracted value **under $7,000** (labor + materials), with a one-time insurance affirmation filed with DOPL when the project exceeds $3,000; trade work (electrical, plumbing, gas/combustion, HVAC) is carved out (DOPL Handyman Exemption application, commerce.utah.gov/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/handyman-application.pdf — GOV DOC; subsection letters (1)(h)(i) "less than $7,000" and (1)(h)(ii)(H) "greater than $3,000" confirmed Sep 25, 2026 on le.utah.gov, Title 58 Ch. 55 Part 3 PDF — GOV). **2027 restructuring (2026 law change):** 2026 Gen. Sess. ch. 42 repeals, re-enacts and renumbers much of the Construction Trades Licensing Act effective **Jan 1, 2027** — the exemptions section becomes **§ 58-55-110** (small-job exemption at § 58-55-110(2)(n): total cost "less than $7,000 including labor, material, and changes," not involving electrical/plumbing, gas appliances or "a combustion system," fire sprinklers, HVAC, or radon), and a new § 58-55-105 "License required" keeps the license duty "unless exempt." Cite § 58-55-305(1)(h) until Dec 31, 2026 and § 58-55-110(2)(n) from Jan 1, 2027; DOPL's R156-55a rule citations (incl. the sweep exemption) may be renumbered to follow — re-check in Jan 2027.

sections.title: What the credential does not test
sections.markdown: Even Utah's real exam tests **Utah construction law, business practices, and trade scope — not flue diagnosis or masonry-defect competence.** An S230 masonry licensee may never have inspected a chimney flue. The B100/S230 credential attests legal and financial fitness, not hearth-safety skill. Individual certs (CSIA CCS, C-DET; NCSG CCP/CCR) remain the competence signal — the license is the floor, not the ceiling.

sections.rawHeading: 3 · Home sale (GOV — high confidence; Utah is caveat emptor, chimney line confirmed)
sections.title: Seller disclosure when a home sells
sections.confidenceNote: high confidence; Utah is caveat emptor, chimney line confirmed
sections.markdown: **Utah is a caveat-emptor ("buyer beware") state.** The **only disclosure statutorily mandated is meth-contamination (Utah Code § 57-27-201)**; there is **no statute requiring a general property-condition disclosure.** In practice sellers use the **Utah Association of Realtors "Seller's Property Condition Disclosure" (Form 10)**, which is **contract-customary, not legally required.** That form **does name the chimney/hearth explicitly** — asking about past/present problems with **fireplace inserts, gas fireplaces, gas fireplace starters, woodburning fireplaces, potbelly/wood stoves, and pellet stoves.** Utah common law (per the Utah Supreme Court) still requires disclosure of **known material defects a reasonable inspection wouldn't reveal.** No inspection is mandated at transfer; NFPA 211 Level 2 stays a NATIONAL STANDARD. So the form is useful but voluntary — get your own inspection.

sections.title: Consumer remedies and cancellation rights
sections.markdown: The **Utah Consumer Sales Practices Act (Utah Code Title 13, Chapter 11)**, enforced by the Division of Consumer Protection (Dept. of Commerce), prohibits deceptive and unconscionable acts and lets a consumer who suffers loss **"recover actual damages plus court costs" (not in a class action except as the section provides) — Utah Code § 13-11-19(2) as amended by 2025 Gen. Sess. ch. 442; there is no statutory minimum and no treble-damages multiplier in the section; attorney's fees are discretionary under § 13-11-19(5)** (le.utah.gov/xcode/Title13/Chapter11/C13-11_1800010118000101.pdf, checked Sep 25, 2026). **CORRECTED Sep 25, 2026:** the earlier "$2,000 minimum" wording appears in older versions of the section (e.g., the version marked "Superseded 5/8/2018") but the string "$2,000" does not appear anywhere in the current § 13-11-19 or elsewhere in Chapter 11. The Division of Consumer Protection can separately seek administrative fines up to $2,500 per violation (§ 13-11-17, amended 2026 Gen. Sess. ch. 95). Home-solicitation sales — contracts signed at the buyer's home — carry a **3-business-day right to cancel under Utah Code § 70C-5-102** (Home Solicitation Sales, Title 70C Consumer Credit Code); cancellation is by written notice to the seller, and the seller can't keep performance/goods except under the emergency/substantial-beginning exceptions. Complaints: Utah Division of Consumer Protection (dcp.utah.gov).

sections.rawHeading: 5 · Permits & codes (GOV — high confidence; true statewide code)
sections.title: Permits and building codes
sections.markdown: Utah has a **genuine statewide code** under the **State Construction and Fire Codes Act (Utah Code Title 15A)**: the **2021 IRC remains the residential code**; **HB 65 (2026 General Session, "Construction Code Amendments") moved the IBC, IPC, IMC, IFGC, IECC, IEBC and ISPSC to the 2024 editions effective July 1, 2026, while keeping the 2021 IRC** (Utah Code § 15A-2-103 as amended; le.utah.gov/Session/2026/bills/enrolled/HB0065.pdf, checked Sep 15, 2026). IRC Chapter 10 governs chimneys and fireplaces. Chimney relines, rebuilds, crowns, and solid-fuel appliance installs are generally **permit work** through the local building department; routine sweeps and like-for-like caps generally are not. Statewide adoption means far less county-to-county variation than Colorado.

sections.rawHeading: 6 · CO law (GOV — medium-high; code-based, limited retrofit)
sections.title: Carbon monoxide and smoke alarm law
sections.markdown: CO alarms come through the **2021 IRC R315 as amended by Utah Code § 15A-3-202** (Part 2, Statewide Amendments to the IRC; amended by 2026 Gen. Sess. ch. 47): Utah adds "on each level of the dwelling unit and" to the R315.3 location rule and adds accessory dwelling units to the R315.2.2 alterations trigger (le.utah.gov/xcode/Title15A/Chapter3/C15A-3-P2_1800010118000101.pdf, checked Sep 15, 2026). Separately, § 15A-5-204 requires CO detectors in certain occupancies under the adopted IFC (NCSL CO-statute table — REF pointer). **HB 402 (2009)** enacted Utah Code §§ 10-8-53.5 (municipalities) and 17-50-327 (counties): a city or county **"may not enforce an ordinance, rule, or regulation requiring the installation or maintenance of a carbon monoxide detector in a residential dwelling against anyone other than the occupant,"** except for new-construction building-permit compliance (le.utah.gov/~2009/bills/hbillenr/HB0402.pdf; county section shown as renumbered 11/6/2025 in the Title 17 recodification — current number not confirmed). So local governments **cannot make landlords or sellers retrofit CO alarms**; there is **no statewide pre-sale or rental CO mandate** (a notable gap vs Colorado's sale-triggered law). A permitted chimney/appliance job is still the natural moment to add alarms.

sections.rawHeading: 7 · Solid fuel / environmental (GOV/DOC — high confidence; major section)
sections.title: Solid fuel and environmental rules
sections.markdown: Two live regimes. **(a) Wasatch Front winter no-burn:** the **Utah Division of Air Quality (DAQ)** issues **mandatory no-burn (Action) days** during winter **inversions (~Nov 1–Mar 1)** across **Box Elder, Cache, Davis, Salt Lake, Tooele, Utah, and Weber counties**; on a mandatory day **no solid-fuel device — fireplace, wood/pellet/coal stove, even EPA-certified — may burn** unless it is the **sole source of heat for an entire residence and registered with the director**. No-burn triggers: forecast PM2.5 ≥ 25 µg/m³ (15 under a contingency plan) in Box Elder, Cache, Davis, Salt Lake, Tooele, Utah or Weber counties — **Utah Admin. Code R307-302-3** (LII mirror, amended eff. 2/1/2017, checked Sep 15, 2026); R307-302-6 separately bars selling/installing non-EPA-certified wood stoves. Fine amount (~$150) and infrared enforcement: REF only. **(b) Wildfire/WUI:** the **International Wildland-Urban Interface Code is adopted** (the Utah WUIC via the Division of Forestry, Fire & State Lands is 2006-IWUIC-based; local AHJs map WUI areas); mapped WUI construction requires **ignition-resistant materials, defensible space, and spark arresters** on solid/liquid-fuel chimneys (IRC Ch. 10). *(Confirm current R307-302 subsection and whether a newer statewide WUI cycle applies.)*

sections.markdown: Salt Lake City / Wasatch Front metro and mountain-resort corridors (Park City, Deer Valley) run **above national**; rural/southern Utah nearer national. Regionalize upward for the Wasatch Front and resort towns.

story.heading: The story
story.markdown: Utah is the **near-perfect confirming case, with one twist.** It **CONFIRMS** the license⇄disclosure inverse-correlation verdict cleanly: Utah runs a **real DOPL state contractor license** (exam, insurance, a public registry you can search) — and, exactly as the pattern predicts, it **pairs that with the weakest sale-side disclosure regime in the set: pure caveat emptor**, where the only statutorily required disclosure is meth contamination and the property-condition form is voluntary. Strong license, weak disclosure — the inverse correlation holds. The twist that makes the page: even under caveat emptor, the **customary Form 10 names the chimney and every stove type by name**, so a diligent buyer still gets a hearth line item — just one the seller was never legally forced to fill in. So the two messages are opposite and sharp: **you CAN look up a Utah contractor's DOPL license (do it — S230/B100), but you CANNOT trust the sale to protect you — Utah is buyer-beware, so get your own inspection.** And the oddball local fact — the Wasatch Front's mandatory infrared-enforced no-burn days — means a Utah fireplace is sometimes illegal to use at all in winter, a genuine content hook. The registered-vs-qualified gap survives even here: the DOPL exam tests law, not your flue.

faq.q: What should I check before hiring a chimney company in Utah?
faq.a: State licensing: YES — DOPL state license (B100 general / S230 masonry-specialty), Utah Code Title 58 Ch. 55; <$7,000 exemption (§ 58-55-305(1)(h); becomes § 58-55-110(2)(n) on Jan 1, 2027 per 2026 ch. 42); sweep-only exempt (R156-55a-301(7)(n)). Seller disclosure at sale: caveat-emptor; only meth mandated (§ 57-27-201); customary UAR Form 10 names fireplace/stove/chimney. Right to cancel a sale made at your home: YES (§ 70C-5-102, home solicitation). Carbon monoxide alarm law: code-based (2021 IRC R315 as amended, § 15A-3-202); HB 402 (2009) bars local enforcement against anyone but the occupant. Where to check a contractor: secure.utah.gov/llv/search/index.html. Then ask the eight questions below, get the inspection findings in writing with photos, and never sign for "emergency" work on the day of a door-knock.
